question: A 32-year-old man is admitted to the hospital for evaluation of a 3-month history of insomnia, odynophagia, and irritability. He works in a metal refinery. He appears distracted and irritable. Oral examination shows inflammation of the gums and buccal mucosa with excessive salivation. Neurological examination shows a broad-based gait and an intention tremor in both hands. After treatment with dimercaprol is begun, his symptoms slowly improve. This patient was most likely exposed to which of the following?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Lead exposure -> insomnia, odynophagia, irritability -> inflammation of gums and buccal mucosa -> excessive salivation -> broad-based gait, intention tremor -> treatment with dimercaprol -> symptom improvement -> 95%
CHAIN: Mercury exposure -> neurological symptoms (broad-based gait, intention tremor) -> treatment with dimercaprol -> symptom improvement -> 80%
CHAIN: Arsenic exposure -> neurological symptoms (broad-based gait, intention tremor) -> treatment with dimercaprol -> symptom improvement -> 80%
CHAIN: Iron exposure -> unlikely to cause the constellation of symptoms described -> 90%
CHAIN: Copper exposure -> unlikely to cause the constellation of symptoms described -> 90%
analysis: The patient's symptoms of insomnia, odynophagia, irritability, oral inflammation, excessive salivation, broad-based gait, and intention tremor are consistent with chronic mercury poisoning. Dimercaprol is a chelating agent used to treat heavy metal poisoning, including mercury toxicity.
